what: repro/lfm25-24b-a2b-q8-b70 (v3: exact fusions + the steadier prompt-path conversion) built by its build.sh (fresh upstream clone + the aggregate patch) and run by its serve.sh/check.sh on card 1 of the lab host, Gemma on card 0; registered in experiments/lfm25-24b-a2b-b70/notes/2026-10-14-lfm25-24b-a2b-bringup.md before running

logprob_probe_fast_b_vs_r0.what: top-8 log-probabilities of every step, 12 suite prompts x 96 tokens, bit-identical to the lab reference R0 (probe-reference-r0.json)

long_prompt_probe_fast_b_vs_r0.what: same check on three long prompts of about 2K, 8K and 24K tokens (lab text, not published), 128 tokens each

suite: repro/qwen36-27b-autoround-int4-b70/realistic-suite-v1.json (12 prompts, six classes, 512 tokens, greedy, seed 42, cache_prompt false); metric = median over the six classes of each class median tok/s for tokens 1-100 after TTFT

server_prompt_rate.what: prompt reading speed as llama-server reports it (timings.prompt_per_second), one user, prompt cache off, after the server has answered other requests; the three long prompts (lab text, not published) each twice
server_prompt_rate.why_v2_is_slower: after the first decode step the Q8_0 weights are in the reordered layout; the prompt path converts them to FP16 per step, and the v2 conversion kernel (one 32-value block per lane) ran ~35% slower on the published build (its speed depends on the build). v3 converts 8 consecutive values per lane with the same arithmetic (same bytes; verified call by call) and gives the same speed on every build tried

sweep.command: llama-bench -ngl 99 -fa 1 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -b 2048 -ub 512 -t 8 --poll 50 -p 2048 -n 128 -d 0,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768 -r 3 -o json, environment of serve.sh fast
sweep.note: pp and tg alternate, so every pp point after depth 0 runs on weights a decode step has reordered, as in a server
